video.title: Fantasy Basketball 'SLEEPERS' - Undervalued Picks On Yahoo, ESPN, & Fantrax

summary: Josh Lloyd goes through the rankings and ADPs on Yahoo, Fantrax and ESPN for 9-category leagues and names players he thinks are undervalued ("sleepers"). He argues that winning fantasy comes mostly from getting value picks and from waiver-wire activity, not from builds or pairings. Players he likes across platforms include Giannis Antetokounmpo, Kevin Durant, Lauri Markkanen, Brandon Miller, Darius Garland, Dejounte Murray, Matas Buzelis, Dyson Daniels, Derik Queen, Coby White and Austin Reaves. He says the best value is usually found between picks 51 and 100. He calls ESPN's rankings and ADPs badly off, which creates big bargains in ESPN drafts. He also mentions an expected-stats (X stats) model he will use in his shows this season.

rules.text: The main way to win fantasy is getting value picks, meaning drafting players who finish well above where they were taken, plus active waiver-wire streaming. Builds and pairings matter much less.
rules.quote: It's drafting someone at pick 80 who ends up the 40th best player. It's not builds, it's not pairings

rules.text: The gap between rank and expected finish needed to count as value gets wider as you go further down the draft board.
rules.quote: So, the gap that's needed to create value widens as you go down a draft board.

rules.text: Turnovers should be punted by anyone drafting high-usage, high-value players because you cannot avoid them.
rules.quote: Turnovers should just be punted anyway by anyone who's paying any attention to any sort of fantasy

rules.text: If you draft a bad free throw shooter like Giannis, punt FT% but get guard stats (assists, threes, steals) early. Do not draft only players who shoot free throws badly.
rules.quote: got to make sure that you're getting guard stats somewhat early. Getting your assists, getting threes, getting steals

rules.text: Rank and ADP affect each other. When Yahoo moves a player's rank back, his ADP tends to drift later too.
rules.quote: often if Yahoo moves a rank back like they did with Davis here, that ADP is going to drift out.

rules.text: ADP is an average, not a median. A player with ADP 50 is going after pick 50 in roughly half of drafts.
rules.quote: So, let's just roughly say 50% of people are drafting him after pick 50.

rules.text: Steals are variable in both directions. Do not pay for a career-high steal rate, but a player whose steals dropped can bounce back.
rules.quote: I told you like that steals are variable. There was very little chance that he would hit three steals a game.

rules.text: Late in drafts, target players with top-30 upside even when they carry injury risk. If they miss long stretches, move on.
rules.quote: when we're drafting in this area. Who else has got top 30 upside? And that's what wins you a league.

rules.text: The best value is usually found between picks 51 and 100, where players can beat their ADP by 10 to 40 spots.
rules.quote: But the real value of where you hit it is between 51 and 100.

rules.text: Do not trust traditional 9-cat total rankings for valuing players. They produce absurd results, such as making Giannis 69th per game.
rules.quote: The traditional NAT rankings like I will tell you again if you want to debate the status of Jaylen Brown

rules.text: Games-played totals mean nothing without context. Games missed because of team tanking should not count as injury risk.
rules.quote: minimum 40% of the games that he missed due to the ankle problems were tanking related. So games totals without context are meaningless.

rules.text: When a player's ESPN ADP is far later than his rank, people are passing on him round after round. Grab him when that happens in your draft.
rules.quote: if you ever see a discrepancy like that, that means that people are in a draft and they're seeing the ranking list

rules.text: ESPN's default leagues use 10 teams and 8 categories, so convert ESPN ranks before comparing them to a 12-team 9-cat format.
rules.quote: 31 on ESPN, by the way, whose default is 10-man leagues, that's fourth round.
